import numpy as np
import torch
import torch.nn as nn
import torch.optim as optim
from torch.utils.data import DataLoader, TensorDataset
from sklearn.model_selection import train_test_split
from sklearn.preprocessing import StandardScaler

model = nn.Sequential(nn.Linear(10, 3))
criterion = nn.CrossEntropyLoss()
optimizer = optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=0.001)
ds = TensorDataset(torch.tensor(X_train), torch.tensor(y_train))
train_loader = DataLoader(ds, batch_size=32, shuffle=True)

for features, labels in train_loader:
    outputs = model(features)
    loss = criterion(outputs, labels)
    loss.backward()
    optimizer.step()

findings.message: StandardScaler.fit_transform(X) precedes train_test_split, so test rows contribute to the fitted preprocessing state. This is data leakage if X_test is intended to represent unseen data. The finding is about the source wiring; no metric impact is claimed without runtime results.
findings.title: Scaler is fit before the train/test split

findings.message: The loop calls loss.backward() and optimizer.step() but does not call optimizer.zero_grad() or model.zero_grad(). In standard PyTorch semantics, gradients accumulate across batches, which changes the intended per-batch update unless accumulation is deliberate. The exact runtime outcome remains unverified because the notebook was not executed.
findings.title: The batch loop does not clear gradients
